Subject: Pioneer DPA redline — telemetry export window & subprocessor list

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team sent over a redline to the DPA with two asks we need clarified before moving to procurement:

1) Telemetry export window — they want a firm max retention for inferred telemetry exports (they proposed 30 days).
2) Subprocessor list — they need confirmation that analytics exports will only ever go to the processors listed in Appendix B, and they asked what happens if we add a new processor in the EU within the contract term.

I attached their redline (Pioneer_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf) — most edits are inline. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 30-day export retention or suggest an acceptable counter-proposal? Also, what is the internal process for handling add/remove of subprocessors during an active contract?

We are on a tight timeline — procurement hopes to get a final DPA before end of month. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Subject: Re: Pioneer DPA redline — telemetry export window & subprocessor list

Hi team,

Short summary of Pioneer’s asks from Emily’s redline:
- Telemetry export retention: they want 30 days maximum for any inferred/exported telemetry (note: they reference analytics exports used for their dashboards).
- Subprocessor additions: they want prior notice + approval when we add any new analytics/telemetry processor, especially for EU-located processors.

Product impact notes (from my review):
- We currently have configurable retention for customer telemetry, default 90 days for analytics exports. Some internal partners rely on 90 days for debugging and usage analytics.
- Supporting a hard 30-day cap would require a product change (retention config + UI/Policy enforcement) and could affect some existing customers unless we make it opt-in per-account.

Security asks (Olga) and legal tradeoffs (Ben):
- Can Security accept a process-based mitigation instead of a hard 30-day retention? E.g., keep 90 days internally but provide Pioneer with a contract commitment that visible exports to their supplied analytics processors will be deleted after 30 days and require explicit approval for any EU subprocessors?
- Alternatively, propose a signed exception: allow Redwood to maintain operational telemetry for 90 days but commit in the DPA to not share exports with any subprocessor outside Appendix B without 30 days’ notice and written approval.

Action items I need from each of you: 
- Olga: short security assessment (risk and minimum evidence Pioneer will expect) and whether notice+approval is acceptable vs a hard retention cap.
- Karthik: product feasibility and estimated ETA and effort to add an account-scoped retention override and a workflow to block new subproc additions for accounts with that clause.
- Ben: legal language options (we can offer notice+approval, or a narrower internal retention carveout).

Emily — looping you in; we’ll come back with our proposed path by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pioneer DPA redline — telemetry export window & subprocessor list

Priyom — quick security take and suggested mitigations below.

Risk summary:
- Telemetry export retention: a contractual 30-day maximum for exports is reasonable from a privacy standpoint but operationally impacts forensic/debugging and incident investigations. The bigger risk is if data exported to a downstream subprocessor is retained beyond our control.
- Subprocessor additions: the ask for prior written approval for adding processors introduces operational gating risk (may block patching or switching analytics providers during incidents).

Proposed security position: 
1) Accept a customer-specific export retention commitment: we can commit in the DPA that exported telemetry delivered to Pioneer’s approved processors will be purged within 30 days of export. Internally, we would retain telemetry for up to 90 days for operational needs, but that data would not be exported to Pioneer’s processors after 30 days. For customers requiring stricter guarantees, we can offer an opt-in data handling policy that enforces deletion at 30 days end-to-end (this requires product work).

2) Subprocessor governance: we will provide Pioneer with the current subprocessor list (Appendix B) and agree to notify them 30 days prior to adding any new analytics/telemetry processor. For EU-located processors, require written approval (can be limited to processors that will handle Pioneer’s exported telemetry). For emergency additions (security/availability), we will notify immediately and seek retroactive approval within 7 days.

3) Evidence and compensating controls: provide SOC 2 report, a snapshot of the subprocessor list, and an attestation that exported telemetry to their processors uses encryption at rest and in transit. I attached the checklist of evidence we normally provide to customers.

If Product can estimate effort for an opt-in 30-day end-to-end policy and a per-account subproc approval flag, I think Security can accept the above as our standard counter-proposal.

Thanks — attaching the evidence checklist and reference links.

--
Olga Petrov
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: security_evidence_checklist.xlsx]

Thanks for the quick turn, everyone. Agree with Olga’s pragmatic stance — we need to balance legal/customer asks with operational reality.

Decision / leadership direction:
- Approve the proposed counter-proposal: commit in DPA that exports to Pioneer’s approved processors will be purged within 30 days, while Redwood retains telemetry internally for up to 90 days for operational needs (not exported after 30 days).
- For subprocessor additions: we’ll provide 30 days’ notice and require explicit written approval for any new EU-located processors that will receive Pioneer exports. For emergency fixes, follow Olga’s immediate-notify + retroactive-approval within 7 days.

Conditions & next steps (owners and deadlines):
1) Legal (Ben): draft the DPA language reflecting the export purge obligation, the notice+approval workflow, and emergency exception text. Target: draft to Emily by EOD 2026-06-16.
2) Product (Karthik): provide a brief feasibility note and estimate for an account-scoped opt-in 30-day retention enforcement and a per-account subproc approval flag. Target: internal note by 2026-06-18. If product work is >3 weeks, we will flag and offer an interim operational SLA.
3) Security (Olga): prepare the evidence package (SOC 2, subproc snapshot, attestation) and share link to the evidence in the DPA thread. Target: share by 2026-06-16.
4) Solutions (Priyom): communicate the approved counter-proposal to Emily and confirm Pioneer is comfortable with the compromise; coordinate for any follow-up negotiation. Target: email to Emily 2026-06-16 morning.

I’ll approve this as a conditional carveout for Pioneer for this deal (PIONEER-4859). If Pioneer pushes for a universal 30-day cap, escalate to me + Sales Ops.

Hannah
